payload.viable_set:
KILLER CRITERION — and it is met, but NOT by the evidence as submitted. It is met because this gate's own red team overturned the elimination that made the front a front of one.

AS SUBMITTED: the front was {X1} alone, with X2 eliminated on the freshness veto (version-control grep cannot see an unstaged file) and X3 dominated on selection correctness. The no-real-alternatives case was argued.

WHAT THE RED TEAM FOUND: the veto claim is FALSE. Version-control grep has an --untracked mode. PROBED, not reasoned about (run-3d8fb30546e5): a file written to the tree and never staged is invisible to a plain search (exit 1, no match) and IS FOUND with --untracked, with line numbers, and context works alongside it. So X2's blind spot is a flag, not a property.

CONSEQUENCE: X2 is VIABLE. The front is {X1, X2} — two genuinely different candidates, which is what this killer asks for, and it is now satisfied by two real options rather than by an argument that there were none. The decision between them moves to M5 where it belongs, and this gate blesses a front rather than a winner, which is the set-based discipline the state exists to protect.

I am recording the sequence rather than quietly submitting the corrected front, because the sequence is the evidence: the first pass chose X2 without applying its own veto; the rewalk applied the veto and eliminated X2; the red team probed the veto and found it wrong. Three passes, three different answers, and only the third one is grounded in a measurement.
payload.complete_allocation:
All three candidates allocate every function F1-F36. No function is unallocated in any candidate, and the allocation differs between them only where the chart left a real choice.

SHARED BY ALL (the rows with one surviving option): K3 alteration, K6 preservation and settings, K7 oblige the review, K8 share the judge, K5 mechanical decision, and the record-search half of K1. Identical allocation, identical interfaces.

WHERE THEY DIFFER:
  X1 — K1 splits into a working-tree element (packaged searcher) and a record element (version-control grep), joined by ONE shared addressing contract. 9 elements, 14 inter-element edges, longest chain 4.
  X2 — K1 is a single element answering both, with a mode switch between working tree and ref. 8 elements, 12 edges, chain 4.
  X3 — as X1, plus a scoring stage between rule storage and packet assembly. 9 elements, 15 edges, chain 5.

INTERFACES = INTER-CLUSTER EDGES, recorded per candidate. The one that matters and is identical in all three: K4→K5 (contract). A rule supplied to the agent and a rule enforced by a lint must be the same rule, or the machine says one thing and checks another. No candidate separates them.
The second, added by the rewalk and also identical in all three: F33 and F34 stay inside ONE element. A candidate splitting them was deliberately never enumerated — the chart records the join re-arm as inseparable, because this project has already run the split configuration by accident and deadlocked.

RATIONALE RECORDED per candidate at enumerate_space and evaluate_set. X1's is fit-per-job; X2's is one mechanism, one code path, one fewer dependency; X3's is zero migration.
payload.criteria_traced:
Nine criteria, each carrying its definition, its requirement lineage and its weight; two are vetoes rather than weights and are declared as such before any scoring, so they cannot be traded away inside a total.

DERIVED FROM REQUIREMENTS: C1←R1,R3,R5 · C2←R5,R6,R7 · C4←R3,R19,R28 · C6←R28 · C7←R14,R15,R37 · C8←R14 · C9←R8,R19,R31,R34.
DERIVED FROM STAKEHOLDER TENSIONS: C3 from the owner's standing one-click bar (tension T6, owner versus engine over dependencies) · C5 from the owner's no-duplicate-code ruling and R13 · C9 from tension T1, the walking agent versus the reviewing agent — a criteria set with no channel for measured local failure will always prefer the elegant answer to the observed one.

TWO WEIGHTS NEED DEFENDING RATHER THAN LISTING.
  C5 was REWRITTEN this pass, not re-weighted. Under its first definition it single-handedly produced the wrong architecture by treating two questions as one job. Its weight stays 5; its definition now requires naming the QUESTION both paths answer before it may rule anything out. A criterion that decides everything by itself is usually a criterion that has been misdefined.
  C8 is weight 2 DELIBERATELY, and the weight was set before any candidate was scored. Had it been higher, X3 would win on migration cost alone, which would mean caring more about not rewriting ten nodes than about whether the rules delivered are the right ones.
payload.front_recorded:
THE FRONT, as corrected by this gate's red team: {X1 fit-per-job, X2 one-searcher}.

X1 — packaged searcher for the working tree, version-control grep for the record, rules by declared applicability plus a report of unattached rules. Stronger on structured output (typed records with spans, against delimited text that must be parsed) and on our own measured evidence.
X2 — version-control grep for both, in --untracked mode for the working tree, rules as X1. Stronger on installability and simplicity: one mechanism, one code path, one fewer dependency, eight elements against nine. Its blind spot was a flag, and the flag exists.
Neither dominates. The trade is real: X1 buys typed output and independence from version control's view of the tree; X2 buys one less moving part and no dependency that must resolve a binary. That is a Pareto front, and M5 converges it.

ELIMINATION — X3 fit-per-job with rules by meaning. DOMINATED on C7 selection correctness (2 against 5), at weight 5, against an advantage on C8 migration debt (5 against 3) at weight 2. No weighting of the declared criteria lets it win, and I checked that rather than assuming it.
WHAT X3 WAS BETTER AT, stated first: migration cost, decisively. It needs nothing rewritten and nothing authored going forward, which also means it works on rules written by someone who never heard of the selector — a real advantage for a method meant to be used by people who did not build it.
WHY IT LOSES: semantic selection cannot be checked. A rule scoring highly against a state's statement may still be the wrong rule, and there is no ground truth here to tell the difference. Its failure mode is a wrong selection that is indistinguishable from a right one.
NOT DISCARDED, DEFERRED: X3's mechanism is the natural fallback if declared applicability proves too burdensome to author. The M5 spike that measures X1/X2's selector vocabulary should record what X3 WOULD have selected for the same states — nearly free at spike time, impossible to reconstruct later.

RETRACTED FROM THE SUBMITTED EVIDENCE: the elimination of X2 on the C1 freshness veto. The claim behind it — that version-control grep cannot see an unstaged file — is false, and the probe is recorded above. The retraction stands in the record beside the claim rather than replacing it.
payload.feasibility_checked:
ROUGH CHECKS PER SURVIVOR.

X1 — FEASIBLE, with one exposure already accepted by the owner.
  The packaged searcher ships per-platform binaries and is resolved through the dependency rather than the PATH; probe P1 established that the PATH route is not available even on the owner's own machine, so the package is the delivery mechanism and not a convenience. The exposure is that if the package fails to resolve a binary on some platform there is NO fallback — already logged as a risk, with a documented manual install as the only mitigation.
  Ref search is proven feasible by probe P2, including its output shape.
  Bounding (timeout, result cap, line-width cap) is ours at the boundary, so it is an implementation obligation rather than a feasibility question.

X2 — FEASIBLE, and its feasibility improved during this gate.
  The untracked mode is proven by direct probe (run-3d8fb30546e5), including line numbers and context.
  TWO RESIDUAL UNKNOWNS, named rather than waved through, and both are M5 work if X2 converges: whether the untracked mode also reaches files excluded by the ignore rules — probably not, and probably CORRECT, since nobody wants dependency directories searched, but it is unverified and it is exactly the kind of edge that turns into a silent no-match; and whether the output shape stays stable between the working-tree and ref modes, since the parser is ours and a shifting shape is where a parser silently mis-reads.

X3 — not on the front; feasibility check not carried further than the observation that its selection quality cannot be established without the spike, which is the reason it lost.

CROSS-CANDIDATE, and it applies whichever converges: the guidance selector's vocabulary — state ids, state kinds, or tags — is unresolved inside both survivors, and probe P5 measured why it is not free: ten ledger nodes carry applicability at all, zero machine-state nodes do, and the field's content is prose written for a person. That is the M5 spike.
payload.verify_round:
BUILT IT RIGHT. Four input states since the last gate, each opened and read against its own claim.

1. derive_criteria — read. Claims: nine criteria, each with definition, lineage and weight; C5 rewritten; C9 added. Verified: all nine carry all three; the two vetoes are declared before any scoring. HOLDS. Checked the one most likely to be self-serving — C9, which I added after being told I under-weighted our own failures — and it carries a scoring rule ('list the observations this project has recorded; no local history scores neutral') rather than being a licence to prefer whatever I already believed. It holds, but I note that a criterion added in response to a correction is one a later reader should check hardest.

2. partition_functions — read. Claims: one relation meaning, classified couplings, eight clusters, qualities assigned. Verified: every listed edge carries exactly one reason; K7 and K8 are new and reasoned; the two strong claims are stated as claims. HOLDS.

3. enumerate_space — read. Claims: ten rows, options pruned with reasons, three combinations seeded. Verified row by row. HOLDS — and importantly, the chart KEPT version-control grep as a Row 1 option rather than pruning it, which is why the correction below costs no re-walk of this state.

4. evaluate_set — read, AND ITS CENTRAL CLAIM DOES NOT SURVIVE THE READING. It eliminates X2 on the C1 veto, asserting that version-control grep cannot see a file the agent wrote and has not staged. That assertion is stated as observation and was never probed. I probed it (run-3d8fb30546e5): a plain search exits 1 with no match; the SAME search with --untracked finds the file, with its line number, and context works alongside. The blind spot is a default, not a property.
  This is the failure the verify round exists for, and it is worth naming precisely: the claim was PLAUSIBLE, CONSEQUENTIAL, and UNPROBED, in a state whose own sibling (probe_assumptions) exists specifically to settle claims like it against the real channel. I probed five things two states ago and then wrote a veto on an unprobed one.

5. THE M3 REGISTER — re-read for the criteria lineage rather than trusted. C1-C9 each trace to a requirement or a named tension.
payload.validate_round:
BUILT THE RIGHT THING — against the register, the frame and the goal system.

WHAT IS WRONG: evaluate_set's veto claim, described in the verify round. It changes the front from one candidate to two, which changes what this gate is blessing.

WHAT IS MISSING: nothing in the register, but one thing in the EVIDENCE. The feasibility check for X2 was written under the assumption that X2 was dead, so it is thinner than X1's — and X2 is now a survivor that M5 must converge against. The two residual unknowns (ignore-rule interaction, output-shape stability) are named above, but they were named by this gate rather than by the state whose job it was.

WHAT IS OUT OF SCOPE: nothing. All ten chart rows sit inside draw_context's boundary; Row 6 option (c), a separate review sub-machine, was pruned precisely BECAUSE it would change the machine's shape, which the excluded list forbids.

AGAINST THE REGISTER: the surviving front satisfies R3 (context in the same call) in both candidates — X1 natively, X2 with context alongside --untracked, which the probe also confirmed. R5 and R6 are satisfied identically by both. R14's mechanism remains an open choice INSIDE both survivors, exactly as gate_requirements said it would be, and it goes to M5 as a spike rather than being resolved by wording here.

ASKS NO CHECK COVERED: none new. The three owner rulings that postdate the frame are all now carried by requirements, and C9 exists so that measured local failures have a channel into a decision — which is itself the correction of an ask that no check covered last time.

AGAINST THE GOAL SYSTEM: G5 again did the work. The correction in this gate came from a round that was REQUIRED, on a claim that looked finished. Under the first pass's forms, this gate would have collected five acceptance items, all of which the submitted evidence satisfies, and the false veto would have shipped inside a blessed front.
payload.redteam_round:
THE OPPOSING CASE, in increasing strictness.

FIRST: the correction is small. --untracked is a flag; the eliminated candidate comes back; nothing else moves. Reopening a state over a flag is ceremony, and the gate could simply record the correction and pass. REBUTTED: the flag changes the FRONT, and the front is what this gate exists to bless. A gate that blesses a front of one while the true front is two has blessed a decision that was already made — which is the exact failure set-based design is for. It also converts this gate's killer from 'two viable candidates survive' to 'the no-alternatives case is argued', and arguing away a candidate that is actually viable is the strongest form of decision theatre available.

SECOND, STRICTER: X2 is only back because a flag exists, and the deeper objection to it stands — its output is delimited text our own parser must read, and its shape shifts between modes. Perhaps it should be eliminated anyway, on C4 rather than C1, and the front is a front of one after all. REBUTTED, and this is where I have to be careful, because it would be very convenient for me if X2 stayed dead — it would make my first analysis right for a different reason. C4 is weight 4, not a veto. X2 scores 3 there against X1's 5, and it scores HIGHER than X1 on C3 installability. That is a trade, not a disqualification, and dressing a trade as a disqualification is what the sycophancy guard names directly. X2 stays on the front, and M5 converges it honestly.

THIRD, STRICTEST: the pattern across this iteration is now visible and it is not flattering. gate_inputs found unstoried needs. gate_requirements found every source reference pointing at a superseded lettering. This gate found a veto asserted without a probe. Three gates, three defects, all in MY work, all found by the rounds rather than by care. The strict reading is that the work going INTO these gates is not good enough, and that a review catching everything is not a success story but a symptom. I think that reading is partly right, and the honest response is not to promise more care — it is the direction the register already takes: move what can be checked into the mechanical half, because the defect rate of the judgement half is now measured at roughly one per gate. What I will not claim is that the rounds have made the input work better; the evidence so far is only that they catch it.

CITED RUBRIC: this state's own killer — at least two viable candidates survive, or the no-alternatives case is argued — plus the set-based rule that convergence happens at M5 and no winner is picked here. The operative test is whether an eliminated candidate was eliminated on a MEASURED property. X2's was not. X3's is — semantic selection has no ground truth here, which is a property of the situation rather than of the tool.

KILL-CRITERION for REOPENING: that the correction does not change what M5 receives. If X2 were dominated on some other criterion at any defensible weighting, the front would still be {X1} and the reopen would be pure ritual. Looked for it: X2 beats X1 on C3 and loses on C4, C6 (equal), C9. There is no defensible weighting where X2 is dominated — it wins a criterion outright. Not met; the reopen is real.
SECOND KILL-CRITERION, on the other side — what would make the reopen TOO WIDE: if the correction reached back into enumerate_space or derive_criteria. It does not. The chart kept version-control grep as an option, and the criteria are untouched — C1 remains a veto and remains correctly defined; what was wrong was a factual claim about whether a candidate trips it. So the cone is evaluate_set and this gate. Checked rather than assumed.

HONEST WEAKNESS: I am red-teaming my own scoring, and the specific temptation here was strong and worth naming — letting X2 die on C4 instead of C1 would have preserved my conclusion while appearing to have corrected myself.
payload.verdict:
REOPEN.

STATE: evaluate_set, and its downstream cone (this gate).

REASON: the elimination of X2 rests on a factual claim that is false. Version-control grep in --untracked mode DOES see a file written and never staged, with line numbers and with context — probed directly (run-3d8fb30546e5) after the claim was submitted as though it were an observation. X2 therefore does not trip the freshness veto and is viable. The front is {X1, X2}, not {X1}.

WHY THIS CANNOT BE A PASS-WITH-NOTE: the front IS the deliverable of this gate. Recording the correction while blessing the front as submitted would bless a set that the correction disproves, and would hand M5 a converged answer dressed as a choice.

WHAT THE RE-FILL MUST CARRY: the corrected veto analysis with the probe result; X2 restored to the front with its real trade against X1 (typed output and independence from version control's view, against one mechanism, one code path and one fewer dependency); X2's feasibility check brought up to the depth X1's has, including the two residual unknowns — whether the untracked mode reaches ignore-excluded files, and whether the output shape stays stable between the working-tree and ref modes; and X3's elimination unchanged, since it rests on a property of the situation rather than on an unprobed claim.

NOT REOPENED, and checked rather than assumed: derive_criteria and enumerate_space stand. C1 is correctly defined and correctly a veto — what was wrong was a claim about whether a candidate trips it. The chart kept version-control grep as a live option, so the space was drawn correctly even where the scoring was not.

NO OVERRIDES. Nothing is blessed past an unmet criterion.

WORTH SAYING PLAINLY: the killer at this gate asks for two viable candidates OR an argued no-alternatives case. The submitted evidence took the second path. The correction means it takes the first — which is the better outcome, and it arrived only because a required round went looking for a probe that should have existed two states earlier.
